options: They provide explicit ordering between groups of styles
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Cascade layers make precedence between style groups explicit.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 34
sections.content: Test subgrid.

interactiveQuiz.question: What does `subgrid` allow?
options: A child grid to participate in the parent's track sizing
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Subgrid lets nested grid content use the parent grid's tracks.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 35
sections.content: Test intrinsic sizing.

interactiveQuiz.question: What does `min-content` generally represent?
options: The smallest size the content can take without avoidable overflow
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `min-content` represents a minimum intrinsic size based on the content's wrapping constraints.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 36
sections.content: Test logical properties.

interactiveQuiz.question: Why use `padding-inline` instead of always using `padding-left` and `padding-right`?
options: It is semantic for writing direction and supports internationalization
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Logical properties adapt to writing modes and directions.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 37
sections.content: Test animation accessibility.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which media query respects a user's reduced-motion preference?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` detects users who request reduced motion.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 38
sections.content: Test animation concepts.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is the purpose of `@keyframes`?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `@keyframes` defines the intermediate and endpoint states of a CSS animation.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 39
sections.content: Test performance concepts.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which property is generally preferred for simple visual movement?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Transforms can often be animated without repeatedly recalculating layout, making them a strong choice for simple movement.

sections.title: Advanced CSS — Question 40
sections.content: Test layout shift prevention.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which technique can reduce image-related layout shifts?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Predictable media dimensions let the browser reserve layout space before content is fully rendered.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 41
sections.content: Scenario: A flex child containing a long unbroken string refuses to shrink and causes horizontal overflow.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which declaration is commonly useful on the flex child?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Flex items have an automatic minimum size behavior that can prevent shrinking. `min-width: 0` commonly allows the item to shrink within its flex container.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 42
sections.content: Scenario: A modal appears behind another component even though its z-index is very large.

interactiveQuiz.question: What should you investigate first?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: A stacking context created by an ancestor can constrain the modal's stacking order regardless of how large its local z-index is.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 43
sections.content: Scenario: A sidebar should remain visible as the user scrolls but stay within the page section.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which positioning mode is usually appropriate?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `position: sticky` is designed for elements that stick after reaching a scroll threshold while remaining constrained by their containing context.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 44
sections.content: Scenario: A reusable card is placed in both a narrow sidebar and a wide main-content region. It should change its internal layout based on the available card width.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which feature is most appropriate?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Container queries allow the card to respond to its own available container size rather than the viewport.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 45
sections.content: Scenario: A design system needs utility styles that can easily override component defaults without increasing selector specificity.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which CSS feature can help establish predictable precedence?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Cascade layers can establish an explicit precedence hierarchy between component and utility styles.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 46
sections.content: Scenario: A button has hover styling but keyboard users cannot tell when it has focus.

interactiveQuiz.question: What should be added?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Keyboard users need a visible focus indicator. `:focus-visible` provides an appropriate CSS hook.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 47
sections.content: Scenario: A responsive card grid should use as many columns as fit while keeping cards at least 280px wide.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which declaration is a strong solution?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: The `auto-fit` and `minmax()` combination creates flexible responsive columns with a minimum size.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 48
sections.content: Scenario: A team repeatedly increases z-index values to fix modal and dropdown layering problems.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is a better long-term solution?
options: Establish a deliberate stacking-context and layering strategy
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Layering problems are usually architectural. A documented stacking strategy is more maintainable than arbitrary z-index escalation.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 49
sections.content: Scenario: A site uses large decorative animations, but some users experience motion sensitivity.

interactiveQuiz.question: What should the CSS implementation do?
options: Use `prefers-reduced-motion` to reduce or disable nonessential motion
interactiveQuiz.explanation: The reduced-motion media feature allows the design to respect user accessibility preferences.

sections.title: Real-World Scenarios — Question 50
sections.content: Scenario: A CSS file contains many highly specific selectors and developers frequently add `!important` to override them.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is the best architectural response?
options: Reduce specificity and establish clearer component and cascade boundaries
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Specificity escalation creates a fragile stylesheet. Simplifying selectors and establishing clear ownership and cascade layers provides a more sustainable solution.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 51
sections.content: Scenario: A developer uses `height: 100vh` for a mobile full-screen hero and sees layout problems when browser UI expands or collapses.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which modern unit may better represent the dynamic viewport height?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `dvh` represents dynamic viewport height and is designed to respond to changes in the browser's visible viewport.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 52
sections.content: Scenario: A component library should provide default styles that consumers can easily override.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which selector is useful when you intentionally want zero specificity?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `:where()` always contributes zero specificity, making it useful for low-specificity defaults.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 53
sections.content: Scenario: Several cards contain title, content, and action regions, but the action buttons should align across all cards even when titles have different lengths.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which modern Grid capability can help synchronize nested card tracks?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Subgrid allows nested card layouts to participate in parent grid track sizing, enabling cross-card alignment.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 54
sections.content: Scenario: A developer wants a component to display a two-column layout only when its own container is wide enough.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which approach best matches this requirement?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Container queries directly express component behavior based on the size of the component's containing context.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 55
sections.content: Scenario: A page has a visually complex header, but the developer uses absolute positioning for every element, causing content overlap on different screen sizes.

interactiveQuiz.question: What is the better general strategy?
options: Use normal flow, Flexbox, or Grid for structural layout and reserve absolute positioning for anchored overlays
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Structural layouts are more resilient when normal flow, Flexbox, and Grid handle geometry while absolute positioning is reserved for elements that genuinely need independent positioning.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 56
sections.content: Scenario: A team wants to create a design system with spacing and color values that can change dynamically at runtime.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which CSS mechanism is most suitable?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: CSS custom properties exist at runtime and participate in the cascade, making them suitable for dynamic theming and design tokens.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 57
sections.content: Scenario: A developer wants a value to scale fluidly but never become smaller than 16px or larger than 32px.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which CSS function is most appropriate?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `clamp(minimum, preferred, maximum)` is specifically designed to constrain a fluid value.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 58
sections.content: Scenario: A developer wants to select a card only when it contains an image.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which selector is appropriate?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: `:has(img)` allows the card to be selected based on the presence of an image descendant.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 59
sections.content: Scenario: A layout works on desktop but a long text value causes an unexpected horizontal overflow inside a Grid or Flex child.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which combination is often useful when debugging and fixing this class of issue?
options: Inspect intrinsic minimum sizing and consider `min-width: 0` or suitable Grid track constraints
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Intrinsic minimum sizing frequently explains unexpected overflow. `min-width: 0` in Flexbox and explicit Grid constraints can allow content to shrink correctly.

sections.title: Senior CSS — Question 60
sections.content: Scenario: A CSS architecture has reset styles, base styles, components, and utilities. Developers frequently struggle with which category should override another.

interactiveQuiz.question: Which modern CSS feature can encode this precedence explicitly?
interactiveQuiz.explanation: Cascade layers allow an architecture to define explicit precedence between groups such as reset, base, components, and utilities.
